passages.provision_quote: Notwithstanding subparagraph (A), if a victim of a crime wishes to be heard pursuant to the provisions of Section 28 of Article I of the California Constitution, or pursuant to any other provision of law applicable to the hearing, the victim shall notify the prosecution of their request to be heard within 15 days of being notified that resentencing is being sought and the court shall provide an opportunity for the victim to be heard.
passages.actor_quote: AB 88, Sanchez. Criminal procedure: victims’ rights.
passages.note: Authored bill sets victim notice and right-to-be-heard procedures at resentencing and parole hearings; it changes who may speak, not whether the system responds with support or with punishment.

rows.reasoning: The only source is AB 88 (2023-2024), which she authored; its operative sections give crime victims a 15-day notice route to be heard at resentencing and cap the notice the department may demand before a parole hearing. That is victim participation, not the dimension these rungs separate — it neither directs the system to "Focus on support and treatment, not punishment" nor to "Impose the toughest penalties the law allows," and it sets no consequence at all. No passage survives relevance, so the row is blank.
